items.title: Blockstream Rejects Ransom After Liquid Network Hack
points: 4,000 BTC ($47 million) drained from sidechain Sunday; attackers returned 3,400 BTC Tuesday but kept 598.5 BTC outstanding.
Company spent a week negotiating with hackers as 'white hat,' then abruptly ended talks Friday, calling it theft and refusing any payment.
Blockstream says it will pursue 'every lawful avenue available,' including law enforcement and forensic specialists, rather than negotiate ransom.

items.title: Bitwise Closing Dogecoin ETF
points: Bitwise is closing its Dogecoin ETF (BWOW, a fund that lets investors trade Dogecoin exposure on a stock exchange) before its first anniversary.
Trading halts October 14, with cash returned to shareholders by October 22.

items.title: Bitcoin Price Action Hinges on Fed Decision
points: Bitcoin at $77,907 (up 1.1% in 24 hours) after inflation data showed annual rate holding at 3.4% but monthly core CPI hotter at 0.3%.
Market prices 69% odds of a Fed rate hike at Wednesday's decision, up from 61%; this uncertainty kept Bitcoin from breaking higher.
From $77.7K, reaching $84K resistance requires an 8% rally; traders favor 77% odds of a pump versus 23% odds of a drop to $55K.

items.title: Regulatory Crackdowns on Crypto Infrastructure
points: Albuquerque city council banned Bitcoin ATMs effective in 45 days, citing a claim that 90% of kiosk transactions are tied to fraud and crime.
EU regulator ESMA flags prediction markets (platforms where users bet on real-world event outcomes), like Kalshi and Polymarket, for rampant insider trading.
ESMA questions why these platforms block some EU countries but not others, noting VPNs (tools that mask a user's location online) bypass the restrictions.

Senate Republicans released a revised Clarity Act draft ahead of a September 15 vote, adding registration requirements for controlled trading protocols (permissioned blockchain networks, i.e. systems where only approved participants can transact) while keeping ethics provisions largely unchanged.

items.title: Sam Bankman-Fried Appeals to Supreme Court
points: SBF's legal team asks the Supreme Court to overturn his FTX fraud conviction.
They call the $11 billion forfeiture unconstitutionally harsh.

items.title: BMTV Launches Monday
points: New video program launches Monday with hosts Grace Remington and Sean Hagan.

Will cover Bitcoin price movements, macroeconomic trends, and regulatory developments, including tracking the CLARITY Act (a proposed U.S. crypto regulatory framework) as it nears final passage in Congress.
